transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Start: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park, Marco Ruiz, Anita Shah, Tom Nguyen, Sophie Lin, Ben Ortiz, Jared Cole

Summary:
Quick sync to finalize steps for decommissioning our legacy site-to-site VPN appliances, settle data retention for the historical VPN logs, and coordinate handoff between IT/Platform/Legal/FinOps. Decision: proceed with staged decommission; centralize logs for 90 days then archive to WORM storage for 7 years pending legal review; secure wipe vendors to be procured.

Topics: scope of decommission, user mapping, log retention policy, KMS/credential cleanup, budget and PO, communication plan.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Park: all right, uh, thanks everyone for hopping on. I know w— we squeezed this in, so I'm gonna run through the agenda quick. We're here to nail down the steps for the legacy VPN decommission, who owns what, and the retention question on the VX logs that the audit team flagged.

[00:31] Tom Nguyen: yeah hi—hi, Lena. I pulled the inventory this morning — there's, uh, three FWs and two old concentrators that still show active tunnels to partners. Some of those are stale but we need confirmation. I put a note in the sheet but I haven't exported the user map yet.

[01:05] Marco Ruiz: before we get into the mechanics can we, like, define the retention baseline? The SOC2 folks want to know how long we keep logs and where. Right now it's kinda all over S3 buckets, some encrypted with the old KMS key. We need a clear short policy for the decommission.

[01:39] Anita Shah: from FinOps perspective we really want to avoid long cold storage costs, so if Legal says we can pull to 90 days hot and then archive to Glacier-equivalent for 7 years, that's fine, but we need to budget for retrieval during audits.

[02:05] Sophie Lin: Legal here — quick note: certain partner contracts require 6 years of retention for connectivity logs for compliance checks. So 7 years archive is probably safe but I need to see an exception list. Also we need chain-of-custody for any logs that are going to be destroyed.

[02:40] Ben Ortiz: just to add, some of the tunnels are between us and legacy customers that have legal hold clauses. We should not shut those until Legal confirms. I can map which services depend on which tunnels but it'll take a day.

[03:12] Jared Cole: operationally, the decommission will need a maintenance window; a staged plan is best — take one concentrator offline, validate, then roll. Also we have old KMS keys that are tied to the logs. If we rotate or retire keys wrong, we could lose decrypt ability.

[03:45] Lena Park: good flags. Tom — can you commit to exporting the config and a list of tunnels and owners to the shared path? Put it in the folder with timestamps. We'll need that artifact for Legal and for the audit trail.

[04:10] Tom Nguyen: yeah, I'll get that exported today and push to /shared/it/decom. I'll include a CSV mapping tunnel -> owner -> service -> last seen. Might be messy, transcription note: last seen timestamps are flaky in the inventory feed.

[04:46] Marco Ruiz: on the KMS side, we have two old keys in the account that were scheduled for scheduled rotation but never got rotated because the applications were decommissioned — some of the VPN logs are encrypted with them. I recommend we create a temporary key policy to rewrap those logs into the new KMS, then archive. That avoids losing readability.

[05:15] Anita Shah: cost of rewrap — is that non-trivial? We need to forecast compute and kms API costs, plus the archive charges.

[05:35] Marco Ruiz: it's not huge, but depends on how many terabytes. My rough estimate is under $2k for the rewrap job if we do it once. The bigger cost is long-term archive.

[05:58] Sophie Lin: chain-of-custody: can we log who performs the rewrap and when? That needs to be auditable.

[06:20] Jared Cole: yes, we can run the job under a dedicated service account and the job logs will be shipped to our audit cluster. We'll also add a signed manifest.

[06:45] Ben Ortiz: question — are we going to keep a staging snapshot of configs before we wipe? Because if something blows up, we might need to roll back.

[07:05] Tom Nguyen: yes, local snapshot and S3 copy retained for 14 days behind MFA. But eventually those snapshots need clearing. We're proposing secure wipe after 30 days post-decommission.

[07:31] Lena Park: okay timeline suggestion: export inventory now (tom), legal review of retention (sophie) by 4/30, Marco to draft rewrap and retention steps by 4/28, Anita to start PO process for wipe vendor by 5/5, and maintenance window targeted first week of May. Thoughts?

[08:00] Marco Ruiz: I have a quick technical deep-dive: the legacy concentrators store logs in a nonstandard format — so our parser requires a light transform. If we run a rewrap we should also normalize the log format to our canonical schema so archived logs are searchable. I'll put a transform script in the repo.

[08:30] Lena Park: good, add that to the checklist. Also note: the old keys — can we schedule a key retirement after rewrap? We need to ensure we don't rotate them out before rewrap completes.

[08:55] Marco Ruiz: yes, I'll freeze key rotation for the affected key IDs and create a short-lived admin policy that only this rewrap job can use.

[09:15] Anita Shah: procurement note: secure wipe vendors — we had previous quotes from SecureErase Co. and VaultWipe last year, pricing's probably changed. I'll re-request quotes and check for FedRAMP or SOC2 where needed. Budget ballpark — could be 8–12k depending on session count.

[09:45] Sophie Lin: Legal needs to format the retention exception template. I'll create a form that lists partner exceptions with contract clause references. Also we need a signature step before any logs are destroyed.

[10:10] Ben Ortiz: ok, service owners — I will map dependencies and post the dependency sheet by EOD tomorrow. There may be a couple of microservices that still point at the tunnels.

[10:35] Jared Cole: about communication: we should send a company-wide notice about the decommission schedule but include a clear path to flag dependencies; maybe a JIRA label or a short request form. Don't want unexpected outages.

[11:02] Lena Park: agreed. I'll own the comms once we have the inventory and the maintenance window. We'll use the template we used for the DNS migration last year.

[11:30] Marco Ruiz: one more security detail — credentials stored in the legacy concentrators: service certs and a couple of API tokens. We need to catalog them and ensure they're rotated before the devices are wiped. Tom/Jared can you own cert/token rotation?

[11:55] Tom Nguyen: yes, I can coordinate rotation for certs. For API tokens, I need service owners to confirm which tokens are still in use. Ben, can you reach out?

[12:20] Ben Ortiz: yep I'll reach out. Might be some fallout with an internal monitoring agent that pointed to the old tunnel; I'll list those.

[12:42] Anita Shah: finance will need an estimated invoice timeline; once we have vendor quotes I can push the PO through. Please tag me in the vendor doc.

[13:05] Sophie Lin: also, if any logs are subject to cross-border data rules, we need to identify them. Some partner endpoints are in EU and APAC. We may need dataplane localization for archived logs. I'll flag that.

[13:40] Lena Park: ok— we're getting into edge cases but good to note. For the meeting close, let's recap decisions and owners.

[14:00] Recap (Lena): 1) export inventory and owner map — Tom (due 4/29); 2) retention draft for logs and exceptions — Marco + Sophie (Marco to draft by 4/28, Sophie to review by 4/30); 3) procurement for secure wipe vendor — Anita (quotes by 5/5); 4) schedule maintenance window and comms — Jared + Ben (due 5/04); 5) rotate certs/tokens — Tom + Ben (coordinate, due 5/04).

[14:40] Sophie Lin: I will need the exception list and chain-of-custody process; once I have the draft I'll propose exact wording.

[15:05] Marco Ruiz: I'll push the normalization script and a rewrap runbook to the repo; it's primitive but it'll do. I'll also list the KMS key IDs.

[15:30] Tom Nguyen: I'll drop the CSV and snapshots, and note where timestamps are unreliable. Heads up: inventory service sometimes returns timestamps in UTC vs local, so expect some mismatches.

[16:00] Anita Shah: I'll start RFQs for wipe vendors and include compliance questions. I'll also run a quick cost scenario for 90-day hot + 7-year archive.

[16:30] Jared Cole: I'll draft the maint window announcement and include the JIRA label and the support oncall hours.

[16:55] Lena Park: great. Any blockers?

[17:10] Ben Ortiz: only that I need a day to map dependencies — otherwise fine.

[17:25] Sophie Lin: Legal will probably ask for minor wording changes but no blocker.

[17:40] Lena Park: excellent. We'll reconvene 2026-05-06 09:30 PDT as a checkpoint. I'll send notes and link to the exported inventory once Tom uploads. Thanks everyone.

[17:55] End of call.
notes: Call felt focused; a few transcription errors when people talked over each other. Important deliverables: rewrap plan, legal retention template, procurement for wipe vendor. Follow-up meeting set for 2026-05-06.
